comparison: Perfect agreement on C1-C2. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers support the finding that AARS2 is downregulated post-MI and involved in MI pathology, based on Western blot and qRT-PCR data.
Perfect agreement on C3-C6. Both evaluations accept the cardiomyocyte-specific knockout model validation, including genetic crossing strategy, genotyping, and tissue specificity confirmation.

Perfect agreement on C7-C15. Both strongly support the comprehensive phenotypic characterization of Aars2 cKO mice showing cardiomyopathy, with peer reviewers describing findings as 'convincing' and OpenEval noting robust evidence from echocardiography, survival, and histological data.

Strong agreement on C16-C17, C19-C24 regarding apoptosis and metabolic dysfunction. OpenEval supports all claims but notes citation C18 should be verified. Peer reviewers accepted mechanistic findings without raising concerns about this specific citation.
Perfect agreement on C25-C28. Both evaluations accept the transgenic overexpression model and its tissue-specific validation without concerns.

Perfect agreement on C29-C35. Both strongly support the protective effects of AARS2 overexpression post-MI, with peer reviewers describing findings as 'convincing' and OpenEval noting compelling time-course data.
Perfect agreement on C36-C40. Both accept the negative findings showing AARS2 does not affect cardiomyocyte proliferation, angiogenesis, or hypertrophy, which helps define the mechanism of action.

Strong agreement on C41-C42, C44-C48 regarding anti-apoptotic and ROS-reducing effects. OpenEval notes C43 as established knowledge. Peer reviewers explicitly confirmed acceptance of apoptosis and ROS findings in their summary.

Strong agreement on C50-C58 regarding metabolic shift from OXPHOS to glycolysis. Both evaluations support the findings, though OpenEval notes C58-C59 are somewhat interpretive. Peer reviewers explicitly accepted the metabolic reprogramming mechanism.

Partial overlap on C61-C62, C65-C68. OpenEval covers broader PKM2 mechanism (C60-C68) while peer review focuses on translation and dimer/tetramer ratio aspects. Both support the PKM2 findings but emphasize different aspects of the mechanism.

Perfect agreement on C69-C70. Both accept the Ribo-Seq findings of additional translation targets, though OpenEval notes C70's functional significance remains uncertain and peer reviewers implicitly accept through mention of ribosome profiling.

Moderate overlap on C72, C74-C79. OpenEval R12 addresses alanine-mediated PKM2 tetramerization mechanism (C71-C79), while peer R10 focuses on translation and ratio changes. Both support PKM2 mechanism but from different experimental angles.

Perfect agreement on C80-C88. Both strongly support the TEPP-46 pharmacological rescue experiments demonstrating PKM2 as a key mediator of AARS2 function, with peer reviewers explicitly confirming acceptance.

OpenEval R14 evaluates background/context claims C89-C93 from prior literature establishing clinical context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers typically focus on novel findings rather than cited background.

Partial overlap on C94, C96-C98. OpenEval R15 covers summary conclusions (C94-C100) including speculative gene therapy implications (C95). Peer R13 focuses on overall mechanistic model acceptance. Both support central conclusions but OpenEval notes C95 is speculative.

Minimal overlap on C105. OpenEval R16 addresses lactate-binding integration (C101-C106) with some speculative elements. Peer R13 broadly accepts mechanistic model. OpenEval notes C104 is inferential and not directly demonstrated.

Minimal overlap on C109. OpenEval R17 addresses TEPP-46 mechanism and novelty claims (C107-C109). Peer R13 accepts overall findings including therapeutic potential. Both support novelty but OpenEval notes C108 relies on established knowledge.

OpenEval R18 evaluates interpretive claims about metabolic mechanisms and ROS (C110-C116). No direct peer review correspondence found, though these concepts are implicitly accepted within peer R9's metabolic shift evaluation.

OpenEval R19 addresses limitation regarding AARS2 regulation (C117-C118) and marks as UNCERTAIN, appropriately identifying unresolved question. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this acknowledged limitation.

Minimal overlap on C119-C120. OpenEval R20 evaluates Abstract summary claims (C119-C128) as supported by comprehensive evidence. Peer R13 accepts overall conclusions and therapeutic potential. Both support central findings with peer reviewers describing 'strong evidence.'
